catalog_quote: (1991: 21) «2.6. Tons. La transcription des tons étant totalement absente des données de RW, je ferai appel ici à l'analyse tonale de MN. [...] MN a inventorié quatre réalisations tonales différentes : haut, bas, haut descendant et bas montant. Les deux dernières réalisations, d'après MN, s'accompagnent toujours d'un allongement de la voyelle qui les porte. Pour des raisons de simplicité, elle considère ces dernières comme des séquences de deux tons ponctuels, et ne retient ainsi que deux unités tonales minimales et distinctives : /H/ et /B/. Ces tonèmes sont associés aux phonèmes vocaliques : tout phonème vocalique est porteur d'un tonème ou d'une séquence de deux tonèmes différents. L'examen du comportement des tons à l'intérieur de l'énoncé montre que ceux-ci font l'objet d'un report. Les hauts et les bas se déplacent de façon régulière et systématique vers la droite, c'est à dire su…

new_statements.quote: (1991:21) «[MN] ne retient ainsi que deux unités tonales minimales et distinctives : /H/ et /B/. [...] tout phonème vocalique est porteur d'un tonème ou d'une séquence de deux tonèmes différents. [...] Les hauts et les bas se déplacent de façon régulière et systématique vers la droite, c'est à dire sur la voyelle de la syllabe suivante.» (1999:121-2) «...les MN sont inaccentués et précèdent immédiatement la syllabe accentuée (par un accroissement de la durée) du thème nominal dissyllabique. [...] Les langues gabonaises getsogo et geviya (groupe B30) possédant des caractéristiques similaires du point de vue accentuel, pourront servir de langues-tests...»
new_statements.translation: (1991:21) '[Marchal-Nasse] thus retains only two minimal distinctive tonal units: /H/ and /L/. ... every vowel phoneme carries one toneme or a sequence of two different tonemes. ... Highs and lows shift regularly and systematically to the right, i.e. onto the vowel of the following syllable.' (1999:121-2) '...[in Sesotho and other southern Bantu languages] the noun-class markers are unaccented and immediately precede the accented syllable (accented by increased duration) of the disyllabic noun stem. ... The Gabonese languages Getsogo and Geviya (B30 group), which have similar characteristics from the accentual point of view, could serve as test languages...'

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Copies checked ( present and accurate; note our source list 'held' is empty but the directory holds the 1988/1991/1999 van der Veen files plus scanned/txt derivatives). (1) Van der Veen 1991 thesis, scan: I rendered pdf page 11 (= thesis pp. 20-21; the report's parenthetical 'pdf p. 12' is off by one -- pdf p. 12 shows thesis pp. 22-23 -- but the thesis-page locator p. 21 and the scanned-file line locator 422-440 are correct) and read section 2.6 'Tons' directly from the page image. The quoted French is there verbatim (report's '[MN]' stands for 'elle' = Marchal-Nasse; ellipses marked): four surface tones haut/bas/haut descendant/bas montant, contours always with vowel lengthening, reduced…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tsogo is described purely as a tone language: two tonemes H/L on every vowel (surface H, L, HL, LH; contours with vowel lengthening), with systematic rightward tone shift/spreading and lowering before pause; no source examined states a word-stress rule. The only accent remark (van der Veen 1999, in passing, in an acquisition-research proposal) implies Sesotho-like prominence: noun prefix unaccented, first syllable of the (disyllabic) stem accented by extra duration — i.e. a hint of stem-initial durational prominence, not a described stress system.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tone: behaviour before pause/in isolation flagged as unresolved (1991: 12 fn. 2, 22); regional variation Mimongo vs Lebamba noted for vowels only.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements concern the word and utterance (tone shift across the utterance, lowering before pause). The 1999 accent remark concerns the noun (prefix + disyllabic stem) and is typological/passing, not based on a presented analysis of Tsogo; for the closely related Geviya the same author describes automatic lengthening of the utterance-penultimate vowel (1999: 133; 2003: 381), and for Gevove longer stem-initial V1 (1991: 66), so B30 prominence facts are position-in-phrase and stem-based rather than a lexical word stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe ɣe-tsɔɣɔ / Getsogo = Tsogo (tsog1243, ISO tsv), Guthrie B31, Ngounié right bank between Mouila and Sindara. Van der Veen's 1991 sketch rests mainly on Marchal-Nasse 1979 (two Mitsogo speakers resident in Libreville) plus Raponda-Walker (Sindara area) and his own notes; he notes minor regional vowel variation (Mimongo vs Lebamba) but treats it as one language. The 1999 accent remark pairs Getsogo with Geviya (Eviya, gevi1235/‘Viya’ B301), a distinct but closely related B30 language; the penultimate-lengthening and stem-initial-duration facts he actually describes are for Geviya and Gevove (Vove/Pove B305, buba? — glottocode vove1238?), not Tsogo.

sources.note: Tsogo sketch (pp. 12-22, read from page images + scanned) treats vowels, consonants, syllable types, stem shapes and tone only: two tonemes /H/ and /B/ (after Marchal-Nasse 1979), contour tones with vowel lengthening, systematic rightward tone shift ('report'), floating tones, lowering before pause. No statement anywhere in the Tsogo sketch about word stress/accent (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/intensité/prosod negative). For the sister language Gevove (p. 66 fn.) he measures longer V1 than V2 in disyllabic noun stems and says he does not yet know whether this is linked to 'un…

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Geviya, not Tsogo, but pp. 121-122 (acquisition research programme) contain the only accent remark found for Getsogo: after noting that in Sesotho etc. noun-class prefixes are unaccented and immediately precede the accented (lengthened) syllable of the disyllabic noun stem, he writes that 'les langues gabonaises getsogo et geviya (groupe B30) possédant des caractéristiques similaires du point de vue accentuel' could serve as test languages. Passing, non-descriptive remark implying stem-initial (durational) prominence; p. 133 describes phrase-penultimate lengthening for Geviya only.

sources.note: 'T, Vo and Vi have in common a tone system with four underlying melodies for the nouns (i.e. H, L, HL and LH) and two for the verbs (i.e. H and L).. Rightward Tone Spreading occurs in T and Vi. In T they spread freely within a certain number of well-defined domains. For a detailed but tentative description, see Marchal-Nasse (1979).' Suprasegmental section covers vowel harmony and tone only; nothing on stress/accent for Tsogo (utterance-penultimate position described as 'prosodically marked' only for Viya).
